marker.step_source:
import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch.  Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# ChangeSpec name -> branch name conversion.
is_changespec = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_changespec:
        # ChangeSpec ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

marker.step_source:
head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

## What I found

The epic and all three phases were **already closed** by `sase-fp.8.3` at 06:40 UTC, so there was no close to perform. My job became auditing whether that close was earned and finishing what it left undone.

**Verification (against source, not just notes) — both fixes are real at HEAD:**
- `sase-fp.8.1` (3e8600168): `tests/_test_contract_budget.py` holds the calibration probe (`PROBE_BASELINE_CPU_SECONDS=0.77`, `getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN)` deltas, mean of a before/after probe pair); `test_contract_manifest.py` now asserts `measurement.normalized <= 30.0` behind `skipif(not HAVE_RESOURCE)` — the wall clock is gone.
- `sase-fp.8.2` (e7917a268): `HEALTH_SCHEMA == 2`; `find_false_negatives` requires same workspace **and** change-set coverage on top of ancestry; pre-schema records are counted and excluded, and the rule is stated in both the docstring and every report.
- Both child `PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP` notes were already filed as tasks (**sase-g0**, **sase-g1**), so no new `/sase_new_task` calls were warranted.

## Integration defect found and fixed

Four post-epic refactor commits split the epic's own modules — those carried the semantics forward correctly (imports rewired, no contract-manifest churn since none of the split modules is contract-marked).

The **docs refresh** (531138373, a7e6f0514) did not. It landed *after* the correlation fix but documented the pre-fix semantics: it defined a false negative by ancestry alone and justified the shared cross-workspace store as *"the point, since a land agent in one workspace needs to see what phase agents in the others skipped"* — precisely the cross-workspace correlation `sase-fp.8.2` removed. A reader following those docs would have drawn the wrong conclusion from the metric. I corrected `docs/development.md:291` to state the implemented three-part rule, why ancestry alone is insufficient, and the pre-schema-2 exclusion that keeps a `0` from reading as "clean."
